opportunities.name: Plan city trip: flight + hotel + tour, then log to Notes
opportunities.description: For a destination city and date range, search round-trip flights from Paris on Google Flights, search hotels on Booking.com, find a top tour on Viator, then write a one-line trip summary (flight, hotel, tour and prices) in the Notes app.
opportunities.site: Google Flights, Booking.com, Viator, Notes app
steps: Open Google Flights; set origin Paris, destination {city}; pick the matching city suggestion
Open the date picker; choose departure {start_date} and return {end_date}; click Done and Search (click Reload if an error appears)
Note the best or cheapest flight (airline and price)
Open Booking.com; dismiss the sign-in and cookie popups; enter {city} and select the suggestion
Pick check-in {start_date} and check-out {end_date}; click Search; note the top hotel and its total price
Open Viator; reject cookies; search '{tour_query}' with no dates (Skip); open the search results
Note the first tour's name and price
Open Notes; in 'New note' type 'Trip {city} {dates}: flight {airline} {price}, hotel {hotel} {price}, {tour} {price}' and save

instances.values: Rome, Dec 3–Dec 7; easyJet €89, Room Roma Nazionale €452, Colosseum tour €54 (an earlier Lille/Paris→Lisbon Nov 12–16 flight search at 65–163s hit an error and seems to have led into this one)
Barcelona, Jan 20–Jan 24 2027; Vueling/Iberia €113, IBIS Budget Barcelona Center €543, Sagrada Familia skip-the-line tour €54

opportunities.name: Compare two Python packages via PyPI and GitHub, log to Notes
opportunities.description: For a pair of Python packages, search each on PyPI, open its page and source repository to collect version, release date, GitHub stars and license, then write a 'A vs B' comparison note.
steps: On pypi.org, search for {package_a}; open the exact-match result
Record the latest version and release date; click the Repository/Source link
On GitHub, record the star count and license
Go back to PyPI and search {package_b}; open the exact match
Record its version and release date; open its repository and record stars and license
Open Notes; type '{a} {ver} {date} {stars} stars {license} vs {b} {ver} {date} {stars} stars {license}' and save

instances.values: requests vs httpx (no note seen being written)
pandas 3.0.6 (50.1k stars, BSD-3) vs polars 2.0.0 (40.1k stars, MIT)

opportunities.name: Answer a browser-support question by email (Can I Use + MDN)
opportunities.description: For a web feature and a browser, look up support on caniuse.com, find the MDN reference page, then draft a reply email giving the first supported version and the MDN link.
steps: On caniuse.com, type {feature} into 'Can I use' and read the version where {browser} support starts
On MDN, click Search, type {feature}, open site search, and open the matching reference page; copy its URL
Open a new message; To = {recipient_email}; Subject = 'Re: {feature} in {browser}'
Body = 'Hi {name}, {feature} is supported in {browser} from version {version}. Docs: {mdn_url}'
Send (the recording shows Discard being clicked instead)

instances.values: View Transitions API, Safari 18.0, to priya@example.com
CSS container queries, Can I Use lookup only (recording ends before MDN and email)
